4º de Primaria · Inglés

My daily routine

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

Si un niño de Londres te pregunta «What do you do every day?», ¿qué le contarías? ¿Hay palabras que ya sabes decir?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

Le contarías tu daily routine (tu rutina diaria): «I get up at eight. I have breakfast. I go to school…». Son acciones que repites todos los días, y en inglés se cuentan con verbos muy cortos y fáciles.

2

Aprende14 apartados

Para empezar: Two days, two routines

Hi! My name is Hugo and I'm nine years old. I live in Zaragoza. My routine is very different on school days and at the weekend.

From Monday to Friday, I get up at half past seven. I have a shower, I get dressed and I have breakfast with my sister: usually cereal and an orange. At a quarter past eight, my dad takes us to school by car.

School starts at nine o'clock. I have lunch in the school canteen at one o'clock. On Tuesdays and Thursdays, I go to basketball after school. On Wednesdays, I have English lessons. I do my homework at six, and I have dinner at half past eight. I go to bed at half past nine. I always read a book in bed!

At the weekend, everything changes. On Saturdays, I never get up early. I wake up at nine, but I stay in bed and play with my cat, Lola. Then I have a big breakfast: pancakes! In the afternoon, I meet my friends in the park and we ride our bikes.

On Sundays, we usually visit my grandparents. My grandma cooks paella and my grandpa tells funny stories.

On Sunday evening, I prepare my school bag and I put on my pyjamas early. Monday is coming again!

1. What is a routine?

A routine is something you do every day, more or less at the same time. You wake up, you have breakfast, you go to school… Your routine is like the timetable of your day.

En castellano: una rutina es lo que haces todos los días, casi siempre en el mismo orden. En inglés decimos daily routine («rutina diaria»), porque daily viene de day (día). Para hablar de ella usamos el presente: «I get up», «I brush my teeth». Es igual que en español cuando decimos «me levanto» o «me lavo los dientes».

2. Morning verbs

These are the verbs of the morning. Say them aloud: wake up (despertarse), get up (levantarse), have a shower (ducharse), get dressed (vestirse), brush my teeth (lavarse los dientes), comb my hair (peinarse) and have breakfast (desayunar).

Look: wake up and get up are different. First you open your eyes (wake up), then you get out of bed (get up). Many routine verbs have two words: get + up, get + dressed. Learn them together, like a pair of shoes.

Vídeo: Wake Up! Daily Routines Song for Kids · Dream English Kids (YouTube) · 35,7 millones de visualizaciones

3. Get, put on, take off

Many routine verbs in English are made of two words. They are very useful, so learn them as a group:

With get:

  • get up (levantarse): «I get up at seven.»
  • get dressed (vestirse): «I get dressed in my bedroom.»
  • get undressed (desvestirse).
  • get ready (prepararse): «I get ready for school.»
  • get home (llegar a casa): «I get home at five.»

With put on and take off:

  • put on (ponerse ropa): «I put on my shoes.»
  • take off (quitarse ropa): «I take off my coat.»

Other two-word verbs:

  • wake up (despertarse): «I wake up at seven, but I get up at a quarter past seven.» Notice the difference: you wake up when you open your eyes; you get up when you get out of bed!
  • brush my teeth (lavarme los dientes), brush my hair (peinarme).
  • have a shower / a bath (ducharme / bañarme).
  • go to bed (acostarme).

Remember: with he and she, the first word takes -s: «She gets up», «He puts on his shoes», «She wakes up».

4. At school and in the afternoon

Then the day goes on. I go to school (voy al cole), I have lessons (tengo clases) and I play with my friends at break time (en el recreo). At two o'clock I have lunch (como).

In the afternoon I go home (vuelvo a casa), I do my homework (hago los deberes) and maybe I go to the park or I go swimming. Ojo: en inglés decimos do homework, no make homework. Y para las comidas usamos have: have breakfast, have lunch, have dinner.

5. Days of the week and the weekend

To talk about routines on different days, use on + day: «On Mondays, I go swimming.» Notice: we add -s to the day when we do something every week.

The days of the week always start with a capital letter (mayúscula) in English:

  • Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday → school days (weekdays).
  • Saturday, Sunday → the weekend (el fin de semana).

Useful expressions:

  • from Monday to Friday (de lunes a viernes)
  • at the weekend (el fin de semana)
  • every day (todos los días)
  • on Tuesdays and Thursdays (los martes y los jueves)
  • after school (después del cole)

Weekend activities:

  • sleep late (dormir hasta tarde)
  • visit my grandparents
  • go to the cinema / go to the park
  • play with my friends
  • go for a walk (ir de paseo)
  • help at home

Careful with spelling: Wednesday has a silent d: we say /ˈwenzdeɪ/. And Thursday starts with th.

Vídeo: What do you do every day? · Fun Kids English (YouTube) · 1,1 millones de visualizaciones

6. In the evening and at night

At the end of the day we slow down. I have a bath (me baño), I have dinner (ceno) with my family, I watch TV or I read a book. Then I put on my pyjamas (me pongo el pijama) and I go to bed (me voy a la cama).

When you go to bed, you say «Good night!». En castellano: no confundas good evening (buenas tardes, al llegar a un sitio por la tarde) con good night (buenas noches, para despedirse o irse a dormir). ¡Y recuerda dormir unas diez horas, que tu cuerpo está creciendo!

7. Saying the time of your routine

To say when you do something, use at + the time: «I get up at half past seven», «I have lunch at two o'clock», «I go to bed at nine».

For the parts of the day we use other little words: in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening, but at night. En castellano: «a las ocho» es at eight; «por la mañana» es in the morning. Fíjate que en inglés no se dice «at the eight»: la hora va sin the.

8. Putting things in order

When you tell your routine, use order words (palabras para ordenar): First, I get up. Then, I have a shower. After that, I have breakfast. Finally, I go to school.

These words help the listener follow your story, like the steps of a recipe. Consejo: después de First, Then y After that se pone una coma. Puedes repetir then varias veces, pero queda más bonito si alternas con after that y next.

9. How often? Always, usually, never

Some things you do every day, and some things you do only sometimes. We use frequency words: always (siempre), usually (normalmente), sometimes (a veces) and never (nunca).

They go before the verb: «I always brush my teeth», «I sometimes go to the park», «I never go to bed at midnight». En castellano: igual que «siempre me lavo los dientes». Y para todos los días decimos every day, al final de la frase: «I read every day».

10. Healthy habits

A good routine helps us to be healthy and happy. Doctors say that children of your age should:

  • Sleep about ten hours every night. «I go to bed at nine and I get up at seven.»
  • Have breakfast every morning. Breakfast gives you energy for school.
  • Eat fruit and vegetables every day. «I always eat an apple at break time.»
  • Drink water when you are thirsty, not fizzy drinks.
  • Brush your teeth twice a day (dos veces al día): in the morning and before bed.
  • Wash your hands before meals and after the toilet.
  • Do exercise or play outside for at least one hour a day.
  • Use screens only a little, and never just before going to bed.

Use adverbs of frequency to talk about your habits: «I always brush my teeth.» «I sometimes eat sweets.» «I never drink coffee.»

Remember the position: adverbs go before the main verb, but after the verb be: «I usually walk to school.» / «I am usually happy on Fridays.»

Is your routine healthy? Check it with the list above!

Vídeo: Good habits vs bad habits for kids · LunioVerse (YouTube) · 4,5 millones de visualizaciones

11. Reading: Lucía's day

Read Lucía's text: «Hi! I'm Lucía and I'm nine. On school days I get up at half past seven. First, I get dressed. Then, I have breakfast: milk and toast. I go to school by bike with my dad. At school I have lunch at two o'clock. In the afternoon I do my homework and I play with my dog, Rufo. I have dinner at eight and I always read a comic in bed. I go to bed at half past nine.»

Answer: What time does Lucía get up? How does she go to school? What does she read in bed?

12. Your turn: my routine poster

Make a routine poster. Fold a big paper into six squares. In each square draw one moment of your day and write a sentence under it: «I get up at eight», «I have breakfast», «I go to school»…

Then, present it to the class with order words: «First… then… after that… finally». Your classmates can ask: «What time do you get up?». Consejo: repasa que cada frase empiece por I (siempre en mayúscula) y que uses at delante de la hora.

13. A day in the life of a baker

People with different jobs have very different routines. Read about Pablo, a baker (panadero):

Pablo is a baker. He gets up at three o'clock in the morning, when everybody is sleeping! He has a coffee and he goes to the bakery. He starts work at four o'clock. He makes bread, croissants and cakes. At seven o'clock, the bakery opens, and people buy fresh bread for breakfast. Pablo finishes work at two o'clock in the afternoon. He has lunch and then he sleeps for two hours. He goes to bed at nine o'clock in the evening.

Notice that with he and she all the verbs end in -s or -es: gets, goes, makes, finishes. And have becomes has.

Other jobs with special routines:

  • A nurse (enfermero/a) sometimes works at night.
  • A farmer (granjero/a) gets up very early to feed the animals.
  • A firefighter (bombero/a) works for 24 hours and then rests.
  • A teacher works in the morning and corrects homework in the afternoon.

Ask someone in your family about their job routine and write about it in English.

14. Routines around the world

Children all over the world have routines, but they are not always the same. Look at these differences:

  • In Spain, families often have lunch at about two o'clock and dinner at about nine. That's late for many other countries!
  • In the United Kingdom, children usually have lunch at school at about twelve o'clock, and dinner at about six. They often wear a school uniform.
  • In Japan, children usually help to clean their classroom at the end of the day. Everybody works together!
  • In Finland, children have short lessons with long breaks to play outside, even in the snow.
  • In some countries near the equator, school starts very early in the morning, because it is very hot in the afternoon.

To compare, use expressions like:

  • «In Spain, we have dinner later than in England.»
  • «In Japan, children clean the classroom. In my school, the cleaners do it.»
  • «Both English and Spanish children go to school from Monday to Friday.»

What do you think? Which routine do you like best? Would you like to clean your classroom like Japanese children?

Lo hacemos juntos

Put in order: «have breakfast / get up / go to school».

  1. ¿Qué haces primero? Levantarte: get up.
  2. Luego desayunas: have breakfast.
  3. Al final vas al cole: go to school.

Resultado: First, I get up. Then, I have breakfast. Finally, I go to school.

Translate: «Me lavo los dientes a las ocho».

  1. lavarse los dientes = brush my teeth.
  2. a las ocho = at eight (o'clock).

Resultado: I brush my teeth at eight o'clock.

Complete with in or at: «I do my homework ___ the afternoon. I go to bed ___ nine.»

  1. Partes del día: in the afternoon.
  2. Horas: at nine.

Resultado: in, at.

Write about Hugo: «I get up at half past seven» (he).

  1. With he, add -s to get.
  2. The rest doesn't change.

Resultado: He gets up at half past seven.

Complete: ___ Saturdays, I sleep late. (on / in / at)

  1. Days of the week go with on.
  2. Add -s for something every week.

Resultado: On Saturdays, I sleep late.

Errores típicos

  • Decir «make my homework»: en inglés es «do my homework».
  • Confundir wake up (despertarse) con get up (levantarse).
  • Poner the delante de la hora: «at the eight» → «at eight».
  • Colocar always o never al final: «I brush my teeth always» → «I always brush my teeth».
  • Escribir «i» en minúscula: el pronombre I va siempre en mayúscula.
  • Confusing wake up and get up.
  • Writing the days with a small letter: «monday».

Ejercicios (24)

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

Nivel básico

  1. Translate: levantarse, vestirse, desayunar.

    Ver solución
    get up, get dressed, have breakfast.

  2. Translate: hacer los deberes, cenar, irse a la cama.

    Ver solución
    do my homework, have dinner, go to bed.

  3. Complete: «I ___ my teeth every morning.»

    Ver solución
    brush.

  4. What is the opposite of put on?

    Ver solución
    take off

  5. Write the days of the weekend.

    Ver solución
    Saturday and Sunday.

  6. How many hours should children sleep?

    Ver solución
    About ten hours.

  7. What time does Pablo the baker get up?

    Ver solución
    At three o'clock.

  8. Complete: I ___ dressed in my bedroom.

    Ver solución
    get

Nivel medio

  1. Complete with in, at: «___ the morning I have a shower ___ half past seven.»

    Ver solución
    In, at.

  2. Order: «I / get up / always / at seven».

    Ver solución
    I always get up at seven.

  3. What is the opposite of «always»?

    Ver solución
    never.

  4. Write the order words: primero, luego, después de eso, por último.

    Ver solución
    first, then, after that, finally.

  5. Correct: «I make my homework at five.»

    Ver solución
    I do my homework at five.

  6. Write three things you do at the weekend.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  7. Write the sentence with he: I put on my shoes.

    Ver solución
    He puts on his shoes.

  8. Write two healthy habits with always.

    Ver solución
    For example: I always brush my teeth. I always have breakfast.

  9. What do Japanese children do at the end of the day?

    Ver solución
    They clean their classroom.

  10. Correct: On monday I go to swimming.

    Ver solución
    On Mondays I go swimming.

Nivel avanzado

  1. What do you say when you go to bed?

    Ver solución
    Good night!

  2. Write three sentences about your morning.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: I get up at eight. I get dressed. Then I have breakfast with my sister.

  3. Write about the routine of someone in your family with a job.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  4. Compare your weekday and your weekend routine.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  5. Make a healthy habits poster for your class.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  6. Compare routines in Spain and the UK.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

Explícalo con tus palabrasComo si se lo contaras a alguien de un curso menor

¿Has nombrado estas ideas?
★

Situación de aprendizajeA day in our lives

The class makes a video or a book about their routines and the routines of people at school.

Pasos

  1. Write your weekday and weekend routine with times.
  2. Interview someone at school (the cook, the caretaker, a teacher) about their routine.
  3. Write their routine with he or she.
  4. Present it with photos or drawings.

Producto final: A class book or video of routines.

Cómo se valora

  • Uses routine verbs correctly.
  • Adds -s with he and she.
  • Uses on + days and times.
  • Talks about healthy habits.

Tarjetas de repasoToca la tarjeta para darle la vuelta

Según cómo respondas, la tarjeta vuelve mañana, en 3, en 7 o en 21 días.

Para familias

  • Por la mañana, decid en inglés cada paso: «Now I get dressed», «Now I have breakfast».
  • Pegad en la nevera un horario con dibujos y los verbos en inglés.
  • Repasad juntos las tarjetas del paso 6 dos minutos al día durante una semana.

Para profesores

Saberes: Léxico de la rutina diaria y las partes del día; expresión de la hora con at; adverbios de frecuencia; conectores de orden (Lengua Extranjera) (RD 157/2022, segundo ciclo de Primaria).

  • Mímica: un alumno representa una acción y los demás dicen el verbo.
  • Póster de la rutina en seis viñetas y exposición oral.
  • Encuesta «What time do you get up?» y gráfico de la clase.

Revisado el 22 de noviembre de 2026.

Qué vas a aprender

  • Learn the verbs of a normal day (los verbos del día a día)
  • Say what you do in order with first, then, after that
  • Use time words: in the morning, in the afternoon, at night
  • Talk and write about your own routine
  • Use routine verbs with get, put on and take off
  • Talk about the days of the week and the weekend
  • Describe healthy habits
  • Describe the routine of a person with a job, using he and she

Palabras clave

daily routine · get up · have breakfast · go to school · have lunch · do homework · go to bed · first · then · every day

Tiempo

80 minutos hoy + 2 minutos en cada repaso
